observations: Instrumentation invokes ActivityMonitor.match in postPerformCreate and again in callActivityOnResume.
A successful match with a non-null Activity stores it in mLastActivity and notifies waiters.
waitForActivityWithTimeout returns the currently recorded Activity and clears mLastActivity; it does not distinguish logical launches or deduplicate later lifecycle matches.
possible_interleaving: First child postPerformCreate stores first Activity.
The instrumented test wait returns and clears mLastActivity before that child onResume.
First child onResume stores the same first Activity again.
The test completes the first child and observes cancellation.
A second launch reuses the monitor and could consume the leftover first Activity before the new child is observed.
current_assertion: launchAndAwait asserts the returned activity is SaveDestinationActivity and not isFinishing. A stale finished Activity would fail the fixture, not convert a production failure into success.
current_hold: All fixture sources remain frozen during the lead current device diagnostic. No new source correction is included in this receipt.
scoped_followup_plan: Keep SaveActivityRoute registered from @Before through @After. Its callback continues to alter only the selected ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT component and returns null; it must never provide synthetic results.
Own a fresh, non-blocking class-specific observation ActivityMonitor for each launchAndAwait call rather than one reusable observation monitor in @Before.
Register that fresh observation monitor before invoking the public launcher and retain its identity for @After fallback cleanup.
Use the real waitForActivityWithTimeout for that monitor; retain current type/nonfinishing assertions and all test-body assertions.

Remove that specific observation monitor in finally, regardless of launch/wait/assertion success. Subsequent launches create a fresh monitor, so late lifecycle callbacks retained by the old object cannot satisfy the new wait.
Keep @After removal idempotently as fallback, and keep actual child setResult/finish, real host recreation, registry, provider and descriptor paths unchanged.
Only apply in a root-authorized scope after the active diagnostic completes; preserve prior source hashes and failing/successful evidence separately.
required_checks: Actual cancellation then next-launch on the device; verify two routed intents, two outcomes and final destination bytes and close counters.
Inspect all eight ActivityResult fixture outcomes and failures/skips.

If timing-race verification is claimed beyond a single pass, repeat the actual cancellation→next-launch sequence under real lifecycle scheduling; do not replace framework events with synthetic results.
